# The `Comparable` Interface

1. Write a class `Student` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `averageGrade` (of type `double`) and `yearOfBirth` (of type `int`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Student` class are sorted in descending order by grade average. Create an array list of 5 objects of the `Student` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

2. Write a class `Employee` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `salary` (of type `double`) and `employmentDate` (of type `LocalDate`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Employee` class are sorted in ascending order by salary. Create an array list of 5 objects of the `Employee` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

3. Write a class `Client` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `clientNumber` (of type `int`) and `lastLogin` (of type `Date`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Client` class are sorted in descending order by the date of last login. Create an array list of 5 objects of the `Client` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

4. Write a class `Product` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `price` (of type `double`) and `productionDate` (of type `LocalDate`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Product` class are sorted in ascending order by production date. Create an array list of 5 objects of the `Product` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

5. Write a class `Person` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `height` (of type `int`) and `dateOfBirth` (of type `LocalDate`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Person` class are sorted in descending order by height. Create an array list of 5 objects of the `Person` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

6. Write a class `Book` that contains the fields `title` (of type `String`), `numberOfPages` (of type `int`) and `publicationDate` (of type `LocalDate`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Book` class are sorted in descending order by number of pages. Create an array of 4 objects of the `Book` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

7. Write a class `Car` that contains the fields `brand` (of type `String`), `mileage` (of type `int`) and `yearOfProduction` (of type `int`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Car` class are sorted in ascending order by mileage. Create an array of 4 objects of the `Car` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

8. Write a class `FoodProduct` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `price` (of type `double`) and `expirationDate` (of type `LocalDate`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `FoodProduct` class are sorted in ascending order by expiration date. Create an array of 4 objects of the `FoodProduct` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

9. Write a class `Music` that contains the fields `title` (of type `String`), `artist` (of type `String`) and `releaseYear` (of type `int`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Music` class are sorted in descending order by release year. Create an array of 4 objects of the `Music` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

10. Write a class `Item` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `weight` (of type `double`) and `price` (of type `double`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Item` class are sorted in ascending order by weight. Create an array of 4 objects of the `Item` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

11. Write a class `Student` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `averageGrade` (of type `double`) and `yearOfStudy` (of type `int`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Student` class are sorted according to a single criterion: in descending order by grade average, and in case of a tie in ascending order by year of study. Create an array of 4 objects of the `Student` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

12. Write a class `Order` that contains the fields `productName` (of type `String`), `quantity` (of type `int`) and `unitPrice` (of type `double`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Order` class are sorted according to a single criterion: in descending order by unit price, and in case of a tie in ascending order by quantity. Create an array list of 4 objects of the `Order` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

13. Write a class `Client` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `balance` (of type `double`) and `lastPurchaseDate` (of type `LocalDate`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Client` class are sorted according to a single criterion: in descending order by balance, and in case of a tie in ascending order by the date of the last purchase. Create an array list of 4 objects of the `Client` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

14. Write a class `Course` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `numberOfHours` (of type `int`) and `price` (of type `double`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Course` class are sorted according to a single criterion: in ascending order by number of hours, and in case of a tie in descending order by price. Create an array of 4 objects of the `Course` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

15. Write a class `Product` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `price` (of type `double`) and `expirationDate` (of type `LocalDate`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Product` class are sorted according to a single criterion: in descending order by expiration date, and in case of a tie in ascending order by price. Create a list of objects of the `Product` class and sort it according to the specified criterion. Then display the sorted list on the screen.

16. Write a class `Car` that contains the fields `brand` (of type `String`), `model` (of type `String`) and `registrationNumber` (of type `String`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Car` class are sorted according to a single criterion: in ascending order by the length of the registration number. Create an array of 4 objects of the `Car` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

17. Write a class `Employee` that contains the fields `firstName` (of type `String`), `lastName` (of type `String`) and `position` (of type `String`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Employee` class are sorted according to a single criterion: in ascending order by the length of the last name. Create an array list of 4 objects of the `Employee` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

18. Write a class `Movie` that contains the fields `title` (of type `String`), `director` (of type `String`) and `genre` (of type `String`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Movie` class are sorted according to a single criterion: in ascending order by the length of the title. Create an array list of 4 objects of the `Movie` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

19. Write a class `Book` that contains the fields `title` (of type `String`), `author` (of type `String`) and `publishDate` (of type `LocalDate`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Book` class are sorted according to a single custom criterion: in ascending order by year of publication. Create an array of 4 objects of the `Book` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

20. Write a class `Product` that contains the fields `name` (of type `String`), `price` (of type `double`) and `productionDate` (of type `LocalDate`). Implement the `Comparable` interface in such a way that objects of the `Product` class are sorted according to a single custom criterion: in descending order by year of production. Create an array list of 4 objects of the `Product` class and sort it according to the specified criterion.

21. Define a class `Client` that implements the generic `Comparable` interface. In this class, declare the private fields `lastName` of type `String` and `balance` of type `double`. When implementing the `compareTo` method of the `Comparable` interface, compare clients based on their balance, and in case of the same balance - based on last name. Then define a class `Company` that inherits from the `Client` class. The `Company` class should additionally have a private field `numberOfEmployees` of type `int`. When implementing the `compareTo` method of the `Comparable` interface in the `Company` class, use the `compareTo` method defined in the `Client` class and, if necessary, take the `numberOfEmployees` field into account. Write a program `TestClient` in which you create an array list of 5 clients and companies named `clientList` using the `ArrayList` class. The list should include at least two clients with the same balance and different last names, and two companies with the same number of employees and different balances. Display the contents of `clientList`, sort it using the instance method `sort` of the `ArrayList` class, and display the contents of the list again.

22. Define a class `Animal` that implements the generic `Comparable` interface. In this class, declare the private fields `species` of type `String` and `age` of type `int`. When implementing the `compareTo` method of the `Comparable` interface, compare animals based on their age, and in case of the same age - based on species. Then define a class `Dog` that inherits from the `Animal` class. The `Dog` class should additionally have a private field `breed` of type `String`. When implementing the `compareTo` method of the `Comparable` interface in the `Dog` class, use the `compareTo` method defined in the `Animal` class and, if necessary, take the `breed` field into account. Write a program `TestAnimal` in which you create an array list of 5 animals and dogs named `animalList` using the `ArrayList` class. The list should include at least 3 objects of different types.
